🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/operator/starter.go (1)
`316-324`: _📐 Maintainability & Code Quality_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _💤 Low value_ **Consider `regexp.QuoteMeta` for defensive future-proofing.** The exact-match regex is built by simple string concatenation. Since `condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType` is a fixed constant today, this is safe, but if the constant value ever changes to include a regex metacharacter, the match would silently break/widen. Wrapping with `regexp.QuoteMeta` costs nothing and removes that fragility.
♻️ Proposed defensive tweak ```diff status.InertiaCondition{ - ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile("^" + condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType + "$"), + ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile("^" + regexp.QuoteMeta(condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType) + "$"), Duration: 10 * time.Minute, }, ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/operator/starter.go` around lines 316 - 324, The exact-match regex in newDegradedInertia is built by concatenating condition.NodeControllerDegradedConditionType directly into regexp.MustCompile, which is fragile if that constant ever contains regex metacharacters. Update the ConditionTypeMatcher construction in newDegradedInertia to wrap the condition value with regexp.QuoteMeta while keeping the anchored exact-match behavior, so the matcher stays safe and future-proof. ```
